hints.title: Keep the equal-area fact in every case
hints.body: Write the two areas as 12AB·BCsinB and 12XY·YZsinY. Set them equal, then use each extra condition separately.
hints.recap: The triangle-area formula uses the angle between the chosen sides.
hints.pitfall: The extra conditions are separate cases, not facts you can combine across the list.
hints.pause: For each case, cancel only the factors known to be equal.

recall.reminder: The triangle-area formula uses the angle between the chosen sides.

hints.title: Decide what the remaining information proves
hints.body: If you obtain equal sines, check both equal and supplementary angles. If the angles give similar triangles, compare their areas using a scale factor.
hints.recap: Equal sines may come from different angles inside a triangle.
hints.pitfall: Similar means the same shape; congruent means the same size as well.
hints.pause: Complete a proof or a counterexample for each condition, then choose the matching row.

recall.reminder: Equal sines may come from different angles inside a triangle.

solution:
Condition 1 is insufficient. Triangles with adjacent sides 1 and 1 and included angles 60∘ and 120∘ have equal area 34, but their third sides are 1 and3, so they are not congruent.

For condition 2, the equal areas satisfy (12)AB·BC·sinB=(12)XY·YZ·sinY. With AB=XY and B=Y, cancellation yields BC=YZ. SAS gives congruence.

For condition 3, the two equal angle pairs make the triangles similar. If their length scale factor is s>0, their area ratio is s2=1, so s=1 and they are congruent.

Only 2 and 3 imply congruence: D.
knowledgePattern: Combine equal area with congruence and similarity conditions
